assurance: Primary-source statements inspected internally; imported theorems are not independently reproved or formally verified. Context references do not establish novelty.

sources.title: Quantitative Riemann Existence Theorem over a Number Field
sources.extraction: pdftotext -layout; statements on printed page 2 and proof setup in Section 5, printed pages 10-11 inspected

imported_statements.statement: A finite covering of the sphere by a closed oriented surface, unramified outside finite M, has an algebraic realization (C,x) over C, unique up to isomorphism.
imported_statements.application: Apply to the connected topological cover specified by the transitive product-one branch-cycle tuple.

imported_statements.statement: For degree n>=2 and M contained in P1(Qbar), the same cover is realized by a curve C/L and x in L(C), for some number field L containing Q(M).
imported_statements.application: Choose algebraic branch points. Pass to the smooth projective model; genus zero over Qbar gives P1, permitting algebraic pole normalization.

sources.justification_inspected: Section 5, page 10, starts with Theorem 1.1 and algebraic definability; Sections 6-15 establish the stronger quantitative model theorem.
sources.limits: No descent to Q is asserted. RET, arithmetic realization, and genus-zero classification are imported results.

sources.title: Permutation groups with a cyclic two-orbits subgroup and monodromy groups of Laurent polynomials
sources.version: Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5), 12 (2013), 369-438

context_statement.statement: Classifies arithmetic and geometric monodromy possibilities for indecomposable rational functions over characteristic-zero fields having exactly two poles. The natural alternating/symmetric case is retained, with many ramification possibilities.
context_statement.application: Establishes the existing Laurent-monodromy context; does not certify priority for this exact double-transposition passport or its collinear-node consequence.

sources.role: Context reference, not an indispensable proof dependency.
sources.limits: No exhaustive priority comparison or independent reproof of the classification is claimed.

sources.title: Primitive permutation groups containing a cycle
sources.version: arXiv:1209.5169v1 (header 24 September 2012; retained PDF has internal date 27 November 2024)
sources.extraction: pdftotext -layout; statements on pages 1-2, Section 2 proof on pages 3-4, and historical justification in Section 3, page 5 inspected

imported_statements.statement: A primitive finite permutation group containing a prime cycle fixing at least three letters contains the alternating group. Corollary 1.3 gives the same conclusion without primality.
imported_statements.application: A primitive degree-eight arithmetic monodromy group with a 5-cycle contains A8. Its nontrivial geometric normal subgroup, already contained in A8 by the square discriminant over algebraic constants, is therefore A8.

sources.justification_inspected: Section 2 proves the stronger classification. Section 3 derives the prime-cycle formulation from Jordan's 1871 and 1873 theorems. Those classical results are imported rather than independently reproved.
sources.limits: Requires primitivity. Finite factorization and specialization-to-generic group inclusion are separate arithmetic inputs, not consequences of this theorem.
